title: Prove durable floor acknowledgment survives a lost installation reply
detail: Canonical runtime is byte-identical to423. An isolated Worker fixture throws after the private installing floor CAS commits and before its reply returns. The app’s injected failure is expected. A separate readonly probe takes the original native permit, freshly authenticates the saved Joined marker and counts encrypted content rows; it grants no semantic authority. The marker must be installing with native floor1 and retained-reading floor1, with zero copied native content rows. Normal retry must preserve the exact saved reading, finish active, copy writing, retain Undo and recover the exact offline cold archive. The declared negative build omits only the private installing CAS, preserves the lost reply and runs the same case/assertions.
validation: Positive native case passes20.4s: authenticated floor1 and zero native rows after the lost reply, unchanged reading digest after normal retry, active floor1 with copied rows, Undo and exact offline cold. The negative case fails16.6s at the intended saved-floor assertion: native floor is null while reading floor1, phase installing and native rows0 are correct. The control-proof command confirms both expected child exits and no timeout. Hash review verifies six exact Worker source transforms in each arm,449 unchanged runtime/protocol files and1,119 unchanged pre-existing test/helper files. Types, quality/format,17registry checks, inventory and10controls pass; the new one-case family is required and every old obligation stays. No full-unit repetition: runtime and all previous tests are unchanged from423’s330-file/3,210pass/one-skip checkpoint. All development failures remain: incomplete recovery-union floor typing and plugin signature were corrected in test files; duplicate plugin composition failed a build; an incorrectly started dependent test stopped at its missing-build precondition before any app ran; an unused build was rejected for a mistyped revision label; its corrected negative build uses the exact positive argv plus the declared omission/outDir. Untimed review mistakes compared independent random reading digests and assumed five instead of six Worker builds; only review tooling was corrected. No app guard, case assertion or deadline changed in response.
summary: A genuine loss after the floor CAS leaves authenticated floor1 before any binary copy, then retries with unchanged retained reading and exact cold/Undo writing. Omitting only the CAS fails the same test at the saved-floor assertion. Runtime449 and prior test/helper1,119 hashes remain exact.
limitations: This is an isolated native reply-loss control, not an ordinary artifact rollback or stale-tab proof. Full floor rewriter/membership/removal lifecycle checks, frozen old Page/Worker artifacts, actual mixed stale-turn idle audit, B fairness/past-index and the same-tree writer-off image remain. Stage5/6 are not complete. No format/trust/server/wire/limit/gate/deadline/default change, commit, publication or deployment.
decisionTitle: Require a native saved floor rather than trusting an acknowledgment return value
decision: Prove reply-loss durability under the same native authentication path that a reopened device uses. Inspect only authenticated metadata and readonly encrypted row counts; let app admission, Undo and cold opening establish semantics. Keep a permanent omission build and all the positive assertions, so skipping the floor’s actual native write is distinguishable from a successful acknowledgment. Keep injected faults confined to test Worker builds.
next: Harden the genuine mixed dense/legacy stale-turn idle-audit control, then complete frozen old Page/Worker and stale-tab lifecycle proofs, marker rewrite preservation, B fairness/past-index and same-tree writer-off rollback images. Continue automatically after each freeze.
